conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way. We’ll use a quick tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s a 10-question screening that helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up in the first year postpartum, so we can get you the right support early on.

Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in immediate danger. We’ll go at your pace; each question looks at how you’ve felt in the past seven days. When you’re ready, we’ll start with the first one.

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[pauses, eyes down for a second]  
Honestly… most of the time it feels kind of forced. My husband will make a joke or my mom will try to be light, and I can tell I’m supposed to laugh, but it just feels flat. I manage a little smile maybe once or twice, but it’s not natural like it used to be.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I can’t remember the last time I laughed without having to fake it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I try to tell myself I should be excited about little things—like taking the baby for a walk or having coffee with a friend—but when the time comes, it just feels… empty. I go through the motions, but that spark of “I can’t wait” just isn’t there anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... pretty much every day. If the baby won’t settle or I can’t get her to nap, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not patient enough or I missed some cue. Even when my partner says “babies just cry,” I still feel it’s my fault for not figuring it out.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

All the time. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly imagine she’s stopped breathing, or I’ll lie down at night replaying whether I buckled the car seat right. There’s no real reason—she’s healthy, the doctor says she’s perfect—but the worry just sits on my chest anyway.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times this week—like yesterday when she wouldn’t stop crying—I got this rush of heat and my heart started racing. It felt like I couldn’t catch my breath even though nothing dangerous was happening. It passed after a minute, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... most days I feel like I'm drowning in small tasks. I'll start folding laundry and hear her stir, then the bottles need washing and I haven't eaten—it's like a constant loop I can't finish. I keep telling myself "just get through the next hour," but the pile never shrinks and I end up crying over the sink.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Several nights this week I lie down exhausted, but my mind keeps circling—did I sterilize the pump parts, is she breathing, will I ever feel like myself again? I’ll drift off for maybe an hour, then snap awake and stare at the ceiling until dawn. Even when the baby’s sleeping, sleep just won’t come.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. I wake up with this heavy knot in my chest, and it lingers even when nothing bad is happening. Sometimes I’ll look at her little face and feel so guilty because I know I should be happy, but the sadness just sits there anyway.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened three times this week. Once was in the grocery parking lot—she wouldn’t take the bottle, people were staring, and the tears just started rolling. Another night I cried quietly while rocking her because I felt like I was failing at the one thing I’m supposed to be doing right.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I couldn’t do that to her or to my family. When things feel really low, I just keep telling myself I have to stay here for her, even if everything feels heavy right now.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – Brief Professional Note

Patient-reported symptoms (endorsed items):
- Marked anhedonia: absent spontaneous laughter, no anticipatory enjoyment
- Pervasive low mood, “heavy knot” daily, frequent crying (3× this week)
- Excessive self-blame/guilt re infant care; cognitions of “failing”
- Recurrent intrusive worries (infant safety, car seat, pump sterilization); nocturnal rumination
- Discrete panic-like episodes (racing heart, breathlessness, heat rush) when infant cries
- Overwhelm/difficulty coping with routine tasks; daily “drowning” sensation
- Mood-linked insomnia: initial and middle-of-night awakenings despite exhaustion
- No self-harm ideation; protective motivation centered on infant

Patterns:
Persistent depressive and anxiety symptoms beginning post-delivery; functional impairment in sleep, self-care, and task completion; no safety concerns at present.

Screening significance:
High endorsement consistent with probable postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety; warrants formal assessment (EPDS, clinical interview) and safety monitoring.
